relevance.rationale: Not a result the folio consumes, but it bears directly on how much a hyperbolic volume can be trusted to identify a manifold — and QOU's mass law m(K) = m_e·Vol(K)·rho(K)/hbar_q^2 is indexed by volume, with Vol(4_1) as the CAL-2 anchor. The paper's introduction is a clean, citable statement of the volume-multiplicity facts (Cao-Meyerhoff: the minimal cusped volume v_omega = 2.029883... is attained by TWO orientable cusped 3-manifolds, m004 = the 4_1 complement and its sister m003; N_C(v_omega) = 2), and its third main result shows the number of hyperbolic LINK complements sharing a volume grows at least exponentially in v. Its own theorems (Dehn-filling families with N(x_i) = 1) have no QOU consumer. Corpus-grep: no ref() entry, no title/author hit in folio/schema/references.ts; the folio's 'smallest hyperbolic volume' assertions carry no source.

keyResults.statement: There are exactly two orientable cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds of lowest volume v_omega ~ 2.029883 — the figure-eight knot complement m004 and its sister m003 — so N_C(v_omega) = 2.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the missing citation for the folio's repeated 'Vol(4_1) is the minimal/smallest hyperbolic volume' assertions, and adds the precision that the minimum is attained twice among cusped 3-manifolds (uniquely only among knot complements in S^3). The folio's phrasing is correct as written but unsourced.

keyResults.statement: The number N_L(v) of hyperbolic link complements with a given volume v can grow at least exponentially fast with v.
keyResults.useForFolio: A structural caution for the volume-indexed mass law: hyperbolic volume is a badly degenerate label for links, so Vol(K) alone cannot separate two distinct link-indexed particles at larger v. Worth stating once as a scope note wherever the folio treats Vol(K) as the identifying geometric datum of a knot/link.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry exists; both key results need a citable source before either can be used.
hyperbolic-knot-positive-volume-via-reeb.md asserts '4_1 carries the minimal hyperbolic volume 2v_3 ~ 2.0299' with no source; this paper's introduction is the citable restatement of Cao-Meyerhoff.
The exponential growth of N_L(v) is a scope caveat on volume-as-identifier that the folio does not currently state anywhere; it belongs as a remark, not folded into an existing statement.
